message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc reported revenue of $1.85 billion for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, up 36.54% on a year earlier and 7.51% on the quarter before [D1]. Net income was $397 million, up 107.85% on a year earlier, which left a net margin of 21.51% and a gross margin of 65.87% [D1]. Communications Solutions Group revenue was $1.345 billion, up 43.09%, and Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue was $501 million, up 21.60% [D1]. Management raised its outlook for the fourth quarter and the full fiscal year, guiding fourth quarter revenue to a range of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion, a midpoint representing year-over-year growth of approximately 37%, and non-GAAP earnings per share to a range of $3.34 to $3.40 on a weighted diluted share count of approximately 172 million shares [D1].

The bull argument is that this growth is structural rather than cyclical, driven by rapid scaling of the AI infrastructure ecosystem [D3]. Demand for testing solutions linked to artificial intelligence infrastructure was a major contributor to the increase, and wireline revenue exceeded wireless revenue for the first time in the company's history [D2]. Management said demand was far exceeding its ability to supply at that point and that the pipeline continues to grow strongly [D3]. The bear argument is that supply, not demand, now determines how much of that demand becomes revenue [D3].

Analysts' tone was slightly negative to pressing on sustainability and constraints, with repeated probing on demand durability and fulfilment [D3]. Management's tone was positive in prepared remarks and more guarded in question and answer, repeatedly returning to supply as a limiter, and the company moved from describing supply management as having no major concerns in the prior quarter to emphasizing tighter conditions [D3]. Management said supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue and that the supply situation is likely to be nonlinear [D3]. Management also cautioned that the one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 will not repeat [D3].

The plan is therefore to judge the company against the guided range of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion in revenue and $3.34 to $3.40 in earnings per share, with a gross margin baseline of 65.87% [D1]. Supply is the variable that matters most, since management said it will govern the ability to convert demand into revenue for the next several quarters [D3]. Cost synergy realization from recent acquisitions is accelerating, and integration is largely complete, one quarter ahead of schedule [D4]. The next dated events are the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference on 2026-09-11 and the 2026 Truist Technology Symposium on 2026-09-15 [D6].
